translations.text: O God of the elements, I beseech you: you are my confidant, with grace. May your face not turn away from me, for you are my judgment without betrayal.
You are my king, you are my law; my heart is yours, my body is yours. I love you, O Christ, without constraint [?], for my soul is yours tonight.
May I not be hiding it, O King: may I be in your royal house throughout my life; may I partake of the feast from your table. Do not leave me behind you, O God. A.
Four did David choose (it is no lie) for the singing of the psalms: Asaph, Heman (bright mystery), Ethan and Jeduthun.
The four, with fair and fine sense, arranged them in the choir; though it was David who sang them, it is to them that they are ascribed.
A thousand followed each man of them, a host that could not be told or numbered, in the one choir praising God. What music could be better in the whole world? C.
How were they sung by each of the four: in prose or in metre? In metre, bright metre, as Jerome relates. Four.
For they were scattered, whoever it was, in the time of the great son of Jesse, in fragments with each company, held in memory among the people.
Afterwards Ezra gathered them in order into the unity of one book; he set before them, clear the method, argument and title.
Why are the titles not taken everywhere with the psalms? Because they were given for this purpose, a pure matter: to express the spiritual sense of the psalms.
The church of God received them in the pure order of prayer, so that from that the men of the world take them without sin, from beginning to end [?]. For.
Fourfold in the psalms, a clear course: first history and second history are found in them (no falsehood), the noble spiritual sense, and the moral sense.
The first history is applied to these: to David, to Solomon, to the persecutors of the hosts, to Saul, to Absalom.
The second history is expressed here with reference to Hezekiah, to the people, to the kings (clear their fame), to Moses, to the Maccabees.
The spiritual sense of the psalms, with its polish, refers to holy Christ and to the church; the moral sense, after that, separately to every fair, watchful, righteous man.
For seventy years in this world Isaiah was prophesying, during the time of four kings, I will not hide it, who were over the land of Israel:
Uzziah, Jotham (a bright pair), Ahaz and Hezekiah; until he went to martyrdom for God at the end of the reign of Hezekiah.
Nineteen years (a famous force) from the martyrdom of the great son of Amoz: that is the number of years there will be until the prophecy of Jeremiah.
He began prophesying for God in the thirteenth year of Josiah, and after that he was prophesying for forty years and a year.
The lofty prophecy of Ezekiel was begun, [?] long ago; for twenty years (lasting tribute) he was prophesying, all but three months.
The ten tribes were carried into captivity with the abundance of their many treasures, the two tribes [?] being made God's own, in the seventh year of Hezekiah.
The comely ten tribes, with fortresses of assembly [?], from when Shalmaneser carried them off: a hundred and forty-two, five years [?], that is in a distinct sequence of courses [?].
Until the strong two tribes were carried into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar: three, ten and two hundred years, that is in a distinct sequence of courses [?].
From the first captivity of the brown [?] ten tribes until the attempt to renew the temple, without any share of error the measure binds us [?]; the lore is true, it is not crooked. S.
Twelve minor prophets are confirmed from it, and four chief prophets who were endowed with the gifts of God through seven causes of prophecy.

Through works, greater than any fame; through signs, many and great; through visions of God in every place; through dreams; through angels; through a wondrous voice, a bright [?]; through the inspiration of prophecy.
The prophecy of the psalms here concerns the birth of Christ and his baptism, his ascension, in every place, his passion, his resurrection,
the expulsion of Judah, without taboo [?], the bringing of the Gentiles to the faith, the magnifying of God's truth, the casting down of every iniquity,
the judgment of Christ, fair fame, over the living and the dead, the resurrection of the world, the sound of the great song. Four things.

Five translations, fair the fame, are found for the psalms: the translation of Symmachus, a course with power, and the noble translation of the Seventy, the translation of Cirine [?], a dear step, the translation of Theodotion and of Aquila.

The translation of the Seventy, a bright [?], is the one we follow. They translated it, a dear course, from Hebrew into Greek and into Latin. David corrected it after inquiry, with obelus and asterisk.

Earnest, dear prayer; lamentation in the face of tribulations; supplication to God, a swift way; cursing with prophecy: these are in the psalms, the most frequent course, for whoever recites them every day. O God.
Three things are required in every part: places, times and persons. They are found here in the song, through the urgings [?] of Solomon's father.
David wrote them from God in the honoured land of Judea. He sang them to Him, a protection in every place, in his rank, in his high-kingship.
Whoever truly recites them will attain the fellowship of the Cherubim. He will not be a son of death after any judgment; he will be in your company, O God of the elements. A.
Ninety-nine, a bright [?], with a full hundred and five thousand, from the beginning of the world, dear fame, to the birth of the Son of God in Bethlehem.
From the birth of Christ, fame without fault, to the year that was not hidden, when the Kalends of January fell on the fifth day, there are nine hundred and eighty-two years.
The number of years, with thousands of valour, from the beginning of the world to the Passion: two hundred and twenty and twelve, plus a count of five thousand.
Eighteen years, it is certain, are all that remain until the end of the millennium. What remains after that, clear the sequence, none knows but God of the elements. O God.
